author: hugh-of-st-victor

lemma.la: quasi quaedam lucida nubes circumferebatur, sicut modo sol
lemma.en: it was carried round like a kind of luminous cloud, as the sun is now

original.text: Ignis vero distinctus lumen praebuit mundo inferiori qualecunque et motum habens circularem; quasi quaedam lucida nubes circumferebatur, sicut modo sol.

english.text: But fire, once distinguished, furnished light of some kind to the lower world, and had a circular motion: it was carried round like a kind of luminous cloud, as the sun is now.

notes: One sentence of physics, and it names the material: the first light is the element of fire, separated out and carried round the world in a circuit. Honorius says the same in the same decade — this bodily light he brought forth from the element of fire — and Comestor's luminous cloud is the same image. Hugh's fuller treatment is in De sacramentis and is built separately; the Adnotationes give the picture without the argument.
